articles.summary: On August 19, 2026, a security advisory was published for CVE-2026-19490, a critical authentication bypass vulnerability affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway. The vulnerability carries a CVSS v4.0 base score of 9.3 and can be exploited remotely by an unauthenticated attacker over the network without user interaction or elevated privileges.
articles.title: CVE-2026-19490: Critical Vulnerability Affecting Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway

articles.summary: In a new blog, Rapid7 researchers explore the operational mechanics of the underground identity economy, using Rapid7 alert telemetry to examine the profiles of affected corporate executives, how these marketplaces operate, and highlight how proactive dark web monitoring can mitigate upstream identity exposure before it is weaponized.
articles.title: Identity-as-a-Service: Uncovering Dark Web Marketplaces Trading Executive SSNs

articles.summary: Security leaders have moved quickly from experimenting with AI to working out where it can make a measurable difference inside the SOC. The challenge now is understanding which use cases are delivering value, how AI should work alongside analysts, and what organizations should expect from security providers as adoption scales.
articles.title: AI is Working in the SOC. So Why are Security Executives More Worried Than Ever?

articles.summary: Rapid7 analyzes KindaRails2Shell (CVE-2026-66066), a Ruby on Rails Active Storage vulnerability that can allow attackers to abuse libvips and crafted MAT/HDF5 uploads to read arbitrary files from the server. The analysis explains the direct-upload type confusion, the HDF5 external storage primitive, how Rails signing material can be recovered, and how the chain can lead to remote code execution.
articles.title: Rapid7 Analysis: KindaRails2Shell (CVE-2026-66066)

articles.title: Africa’s Cybersecurity Challenge Is Bigger Than Access to Technology

articles.summary: Rapid7 Labs conducted a zero-day research project against Microsoft SharePoint, resulting in the discovery of two new vulnerabilities that, when chained together, achieve unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) against a vulnerable SharePoint server. Today, both Rapid7 and Microsoft are disclosing the second vulnerability in this chain, the RCE vulnerability CVE-2026-63520.
articles.title: CVE-2026-63520: Microsoft SharePoint Remote Code Execution (FIXED)

articles.summary: On August 2, 2026, N-able published a security advisory for CVE-2026-18577, an authentication bypass vulnerability affecting N-central that was discovered being exploited in-the-wild after an incomplete fix for an earlier authentication bypass issue, CVE-2026-18556 was disclosed. CVE-2026-18577 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and obtain administrative control of vulnerable N-central servers in affected deployments.
articles.title: CVE-2026-18577: N-able N-central Authentication Bypass Exploited in the Wild

articles.summary: This wrap-up brings a full-on shell parade. Thirteen shiny new modules landed, starting with a buffet of RCEs. WordPress WP2Shell, Ghost CMS, Joomla JCE, Langflow, OpenCATS, Pterodactyl Panel, SonicWall SMA1000, Ray Dashboard, a Pix-for-WooCommerce, and for those who like their exploits closer to the bare-metal, the Fragnesia Linux kernel LPE (CVE-2026-46300). Metasploit also got the glow-up of the summer with the new http malleable profiles, MCP functionality and linux multi fetch payloads (more details on the official 6.5 release blog post!). Windows on ARM confirm to be the new first-class citizenship thanks to brand-new AArch64 reverse-TCP shells (both inline and staged), so your Snapdragon boxes can join the party too. Last but not least, an important message: Nyan Nyan Nyan Nyan Nyan Nyan.
articles.title: Metasploit Wrap Up: Lot of summer shells and fit http profiles

articles.summary: Rapid7 Labs identified an exposed web directory on infrastructure used to support a cryptocurrency fraud operation. Raw phone-number datasets, phishing panels, voice-dialing scripts & more, alongside evidence that the operator relied on AI coding assistants throughout the campaign's development, together provide an unusual view into AI's impact on modern scams.
articles.title: Operation ASTERIX: Anatomy of a Crypto Fraud Pipeline
